newsitem.title: USA: China may have bought U.S. soybeans-U.S. exporters.
newsitem.headline: China may have bought U.S. soybeans-U.S. exporters.

text.p: China appeared to have bought at least one cargo of U.S. soybeans and possibly two more on Thursday night, several U.S. exporters said.
"I think at least one cargo has been confirmed" for May/June delivery, one U.S. exporter said. The exporter said one cargo was about 50,000 to 55,000 tonnes.
Regarding the other two cargoes, the exporter added, "it was a pretty good guess it was done."
Soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade surged in fast dealings amid talk China bought U.S. soybeans, traders said.
Another U.S. exporter said he believed the sale was done but did not know the amount.
"We are of the opinion that they have bought a cargo or so. We were aware of one FOB trade. We were told delivery was set for May/July delivery. Perhaps the Chinese are long beans," he said.
But the exporter stressed that he has not seen any sales registrations.
On the other hand, several exporters and traders said the sale did not make much economic sense since Brazilian beans were cheaper than U.S. soybeans.
"The rumor was for between one and three cargoes," a third U.S. exporter said. "I think that none has been done."
He noted for a June position, the net FOB basis for Brazilian soybeans was about 16-1/2 cents over the July Chicago Board of Trade contract.
"In the United States, to buy a June position you pay a minimum 27 cents if not more, over the July. So it seems to me we are talking 10 cents (a bushel difference) maybe even more," he said.
One major soybean trader was also skeptical about the sale although he pointed out U.S. soybeans can be loaded immediately.
"We do have immediate availability and there is a 25- to 30-day wait in South America," he said.
